headline: Dry through Thursday as Central Kentucky nears 90 and the Upstate warms into the upper 80s
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: High pressure keeps Danville and the Bluegrass dry through Thursday. Light easterly wind today becomes southerly Wednesday and Thursday, driving a rapid warm-up from around 80 today to near 90 Thursday while overnight temperatures also turn much milder.

days.label: Tuesday
days.forecast: Sunny and dry after the cool start, with a light east wind near 2–5 mph. A few high clouds may arrive tonight, but conditions remain mostly clear to partly cloudy as temperatures settle into the middle to upper 50s.

days.label: Wednesday
days.forecast: Mostly sunny and distinctly warmer as southerly return flow develops. South wind increases to around 5–10 mph during the afternoon. Wednesday night remains mostly clear and dry, with temperatures holding in the lower 60s.

days.label: Thursday
days.hazard: No official hazard expected; afternoon heat approaches 90°F
days.forecast: Mostly sunny, hot for early October and increasingly humid. South wind runs about 7–12 mph. Thursday night stays dry and partly cloudy through the end of the 72-hour period, with unusually mild lows in the upper 60s.

kentucky.bottomLine: Confidence is high that Central Kentucky stays dry through Thursday. The main forecast feature is the sharp warm-up, culminating near 90 Thursday. Rain associated with an approaching cold front is expected to wait until Friday, beyond this 72-hour window.
kentucky.confidence: High on dry weather; moderate-high on the exact Thursday maximum temperature

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson / Central primary · Tempest excluded
upstate.summary: Clemson and Central remain sunny and dry through Thursday as weak high pressure shifts offshore. Afternoon temperatures rise from the lower 80s today to the upper 80s Thursday, while light wind and mostly clear nights continue.

currentConditions.condition: Network observations are WeatherFlow–Tempest-fed and excluded; official KCEU and KLQK observations used instead

days.label: Tuesday
days.forecast: Sunny and dry with a light east wind around 2–5 mph. Clear skies and nearly calm wind tonight support a comfortable morning low in the middle to upper 50s.

days.label: Wednesday
days.forecast: Sunny and warmer with a very light east-southeast wind. Moisture return remains weak, so no afternoon convection is expected. Wednesday night stays mostly clear with lows near the upper 50s.

days.label: Thursday
days.forecast: Sunny, dry and warmer, with afternoon temperatures reaching the upper 80s. Wind remains light and variable. Thursday night remains mostly clear and dry through the end of the forecast window, although humidity begins to rise.

upstate.bottomLine: Confidence is high in dry, mostly sunny weather through Thursday. The warming trend continues, but organized rain is expected to hold off until the weekend, well beyond this forecast window.

sourceNotes: NWS point forecasts for Danville and Clemson were generated at 7:38 AM EDT. Official airport observations span 6:55–7:20 AM EDT.

The Louisville and Greenville-Spartanburg Area Forecast Discussions were issued at 7:12 AM and 6:31 AM EDT, respectively. Louisville supports dry weather through Thursday, a strong warming trend and rain arriving Friday. Greenville-Spartanburg supports dry weather through Thursday and delays widespread Upstate rain until Saturday.
The NWS active-alert API returned no active alerts for either the Danville or Clemson forecast point at the 7:37 AM EDT check. This official-alert status is separate from the independent analysis.

Model inventories checked before issuance showed the 10Z HRRR complete through forecast hour 18, the 10Z RAP through hour 21, 06Z NAM through hour 84, NAM 3-km Nest through hour 60, 06Z GFS through hour 384, and the 06Z GEFS mean through hour 264. The latest complete ECMWF deterministic cycle available for verification was 00Z through hour 360.

College of DuPage NEXLAB imagery was checked directly. The 11:31 AM UTC visible satellite showed both forecast regions largely clear, and the 11:35 AM UTC Southeast radar mosaic showed no organized echoes over either region.

Clemson Weather Network identifies its observations as WeatherFlow–Tempest data. Those observations were excluded, and official KCEU and KLQK observations were used for Upstate analysis and verification.
Radar and satellite links remain external and live; the existing Google Sites radar section is not modified by this candidate.
